vocabulary.meaning: money that a person or organisation owes
examples: Many households struggle to repay debt.
Too much debt can create long-term financial stress.

vocabulary.meaning: money borrowed from a bank or another person that must be repaid
examples: She took out a loan to pay for university.
The bank refused to give him another loan.
High interest can make a loan much more expensive.
The borrower pays interest every month.

vocabulary.meaning: money paid back as part of a debt
examples: He missed two loan repayments after losing his job.
The bank agreed to reduce the monthly repayment.

vocabulary.meaning: a person or organisation that is owed money
examples: The company negotiated with its creditors.
A creditor may take legal action if a debt is not paid.

vocabulary.meaning: a person or organisation that borrows money
examples: The borrower must understand the terms of the loan.
Responsible lenders check whether a borrower can afford repayments.

vocabulary.meaning: a plan for how much money you will earn and spend
examples: A monthly budget can help people control their spending.
They changed their budget after prices increased.

vocabulary.meaning: failure to repay money that is owed
examples: The company was at risk of default on its loans.
A serious financial crisis can cause borrowers to default.

vocabulary.meaning: to have enough money to pay for something
examples: Some families cannot afford higher monthly repayments.
Before borrowing, ask whether you can afford the loan.

vocabulary.meaning: a cost or debt that causes financial difficulty
examples: Medical bills became a major financial burden for the family.
High-interest debt can be a heavy financial burden.
